title: Delhi Capitals Owner Ends KL Rahul Trade Speculation Ahead of IPL 2027
excerpt: Co-owner Parth Jindal declared 'we have unfinished business' after weeks of rumours linking the 34-year-old batter with Kolkata Knight Riders.
body:
• Delhi Capitals co-owner Parth Jindal publicly confirmed KL Rahul will stay with the franchise for IPL 2027, shutting down trade rumours linking him with KKR.
  • Rahul scored 593 runs in IPL 2026 at a strike rate of 174.41, finishing as DC's leading run-scorer for the second consecutive season.
  • JSW Group's Parth Jindal will take full operational control of DC's men's team from IPL 2027, with GMR Group shifting to the women's WPL side.
  • Rishabh Pant's return to DC from Lucknow Super Giants had fuelled speculation about Rahul's role in the squad.

Delhi Capitals co-owner Parth Jindal has put an end to weeks of trade speculation surrounding KL Rahul, declaring on X on Sunday that the India Test vice-captain is going nowhere ahead of IPL 2027.

Rumours of a potential swap with Kolkata Knight Riders had gathered momentum on social media over the past fortnight. Reports also surfaced about a reported dressing-room clash between Rahul and DC head coach Hemang Badani during the 2026 season. Neither the franchise nor Rahul had officially addressed the speculation until Jindal broke his silence.

"KL IS KLUTCH FOR @DelhiCapitals — one of the nicest guys I know and one who puts the team before himself always. We have unfinished business and will work hard together to make Delhi proud."

— Parth Jindal, Delhi Capitals co-owner

Rahul responded on X: "Thank you, can't wait for the coming season."

Two Strong Seasons With Delhi

The 34-year-old Karnataka batter has been Delhi's most consistent performer since joining ahead of IPL 2025, when the franchise outbid Chennai Super Kings, Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Kolkata Knight Riders at the mega auction. DC retained him for Rs 14 crore before the 2026 season.

In IPL 2026, Rahul scored 593 runs across 14 matches at an average of 45.61 and a strike rate of 174.41, recording one century and five half-centuries. That followed 539 runs in his debut DC season in 2025, including the highest individual score by an Indian in IPL history. Across both seasons, he has been the franchise's undisputed top scorer.

The Pant Factor

Trade rumours intensified after Rishabh Pant completed a high-profile return to Delhi Capitals from Lucknow Super Giants, with left-arm spinner Kuldeep Yadav going the other way. Pant, who started his IPL career with Delhi in 2016, is set for a homecoming after a two-year stint in Lucknow.

With Pant taking over wicketkeeping duties, Rahul is expected to focus as a specialist batter at the top of the order. The combination of two of India's most explosive batters could strengthen a DC lineup that finished sixth in 2026 with seven wins and seven losses, falling short of the playoffs under captain Axar Patel.

Ownership Transition

The timing of Jindal's intervention is notable. DC is jointly owned by GMR Group and JSW, with the two conglomerates rotating operational control of the men's team every two years. From IPL 2027, Jindal's JSW Group takes charge of the men's side while GMR shifts to the Women's Premier League team.

Jindal's personal connection with Rahul predates the DC signing. In a post-auction interview in 2025, Jindal noted that Rahul, a Bengaluru native, had attended matches of Bengaluru FC, the Indian Super League football club that Jindal owns.

What's Next

Delhi Capitals also released a video of Rahul addressing fans directly, telling supporters to "keep the noise coming" and expressing eagerness for the 2027 campaign. With Pant and Rahul now in the same squad, DC will look to end their wait for a maiden IPL title. The franchise's best finish remains the runners-up spot in 2020, and the Jindal-led management will face immediate pressure to deliver results with arguably the strongest Indian batting core in the league.
